content.text:
This PR is essentially a rebuild of mise’s CLI documentation system.

It:

- Corrects inaccurate or stale `--help` text and examples across many commands.
- Regenerates all 191 CLI reference pages, the man page, `mise.usage.kdl`, and `llms.txt`.
- Adds a post-processor that:
  - distinguishes required `<SUBCOMMAND>` from optional `[SUBCOMMAND]`
  - fixes `mise run [TASK] [ARGS]…`
  - converts examples into proper fenced code blocks
  - adds “Related documentation” navigation
  - groups the root command index by workflow
- Adds tests to ensure that generated formatting remains correct.

The huge diff—263 files, roughly 4,200 additions—is predominantly generated documentation.

There is one real behavioral change hiding under the docs title: concurrent `mise install-into` operations targeting the same destination are now serialized with a destination lock. This prevents two cooperating `install-into` processes from checking/replacing the same directory simultaneously. The lock acquisition runs on a blocking worker so it doesn’t stall Tokio’s async runtime.

So, in one sentence: **it makes the CLI reference much more accurate and navigable, while also fixing a narrow `install-into` concurrency race.**

The PR is currently open and its GitHub checks are green: [jdx/mise#12885](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12885).

content.text:
Yes—several patches are compensating for generic shortcomings in usage and would be better fixed here.

The clearest candidates are:

- **Optional subcommand syntax.** Rendering `[SUBCOMMAND]` when `subcommand_required=false` is generic behavior. usage already carries that field, but [`SpecCommand::usage()`](/Users/jdx/src/usage/lib/src/spec/cmd.rs:818) always emits `<SUBCOMMAND>`. I’d introduce a documentation/display synopsis rather than change the parser-facing usage representation unexpectedly.
- **Indented blocks → fenced code.** The current implementation in [`fence_indented_blocks()`](/Users/jdx/src/usage/lib/src/docs/markdown/renderer.rs:328) is line-based and cannot correctly distinguish nested lists, existing fences, JSON/TOML indentation, or embedded backticks. The mise Markdown-aware implementation and regression tests belong here.
- **Missing `## Subcommands` with a hidden first child.** That is a generic template bug: the template checks `loop.first` after iterating over all children, including hidden ones. It should filter visible commands before iterating.
- **Mounted-command synopsis.** The hardcoded `mise run [TASK] [ARGS]…` patch exposes usage’s existing `// TODO: mounts?`. The real fix belongs in usage, although it needs proper mount metadata or resolution—not special-casing `mise tasks --usage`.
- **Link output format.** Hardcoding `.html` is VitePress-specific, but usage could support something like `--link-extension=.html` or a link template. Its default should probably remain `.md`.
- Possibly **promoting help-text `Examples:` into a heading**, although structured `example` nodes are the cleaner long-term solution.

These should remain in mise:

- workflow-based command categories
- command-to-guide mappings and “Related documentation”
- compatibility-spelling explanations
- mise-specific introductory prose
- corrections to individual command descriptions/examples
- the `install-into` locking fix

My preferred shape would be to upstream the generic renderer fixes into usage, release usage, then shrink `cli-reference.ts` to mise’s navigation/editorial layer. That would remove the most fragile Markdown surgery from mise and make the improvements available to every usage-generated reference. [PR #12885](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12885) is currently mixing those two layers.
